title: Cap. II Arg. 5: 1 Tim. 2:4 — common will to save all grounds foresight-election
pass_a_gloss: Fifth, from 1 Tim. ii. 4. God wills all men to be saved, they argue in this way: that God, from this common will of saving all, gives to all sufficient grace by which they may be led to salvation. That therefore he elects some to glory and passes by others comes to pass because he foresees that some will cooperate with this grace and persevere in holiness, but others either will not cooperate at all, or will not remain in good works and faith: Therefore there is no election to glory except from foresight of merits.
pass_b_english: Fifth: from 1 Timothy 2:4 — "God wills all men to be saved" — they argue that from this common will to save all, God gives everyone sufficient grace to reach salvation. So some are elect to glory and others passed by only because he foresaw who would cooperate with that grace and persevere in holiness, and who would not cooperate at all, or would not remain in good works and faith. Therefore, they say, there is no election to glory except from foresight of merits.
source_text: Quinto, ex 1 Timoth. ii. 4. Deus vult omnes homines salvos fieri, hunc in modum argumentantur, Deum ex hac communi voluntate salvandi omnes, dare omnibus sufficientem gratiam qua ad salutem perducantur. Quod itaque quosdam eligit ad gloriam, quosdam praeterit, id inde evenire, quod praevideat quosdam cooperaturos huic gratiae & in sanctitate perseveraturos, quosdam aut non omnino cooperaturos, aut in bonis operibus & fide non permansuros: Ergo nulla est electio ad gloriam nisi ex praescientia meritorum.
